subject: Sunrise Health POC — success terms, ops handoff & acceptance routes
body:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sunrise Health POC — success terms, ops handoff & acceptance routes

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a proposed operational route so we can lock the POC timeline.

Summary of what Sunrise wants to validate during the POC:
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 350ms for 512-token prompts (avg seq length ~200–300).
- Throughput: sustained 120 requests/minute during peak windows, burst to 300/min for 30s.
- Cost: target cost/token that keeps estimated monthly bill under $4k for the test workload (we're showing options for quantized model variants).
- Quality: automated evals on the seed prompt set with at least 92% pass rate on relevance + safety checks; manual review for 200 samples.

Proposed POC structure (operational route):
1) Week 0 (this week) — Access + sample workload ingestion: Sunrise provides 1k representative prompts and labels. Redwood provides test credentials and a sandbox endpoint.
2) Week 1 — Baseline run (unoptimized model): capture latency/throughput/cost and baseline quality.
3) Week 2 — Performance tuning: enable batching, KV caching, and try 4-bit quantized variant; measure improvements.
4) Week 3 — Stress run + acceptance readout: run scheduled high-load windows and produce KPI readout.
5) Week 4 — Final review and ops handoff, decision (go/no-go).

Owners (Redwood):
- Technical lead / bench tests: Ben Carter — ben_carter@redwood.ai
- Onboarding / infra access & billing: Monica Patel — monica_patel@redwood.ai
- AE / coordination: David Kim — david.kim@redwood.ai

Owners (Sunrise):
- Buyer exec: Rajiv Nair
- Technical contact: Alicia Chen
- Procurement: procurement@sunrisehealth.com

Key acceptance criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms for 512-token prompts during normal traffic; no more than 5% of requests > 600ms during stress windows.
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/min with burst handling up to 300 req/min for up to 30s (no errors > 1%).
- Cost: an example cost breakdown for the measured run that results in projected monthly < $4k — thresholds to be confirmed after baseline run.
- Quality: automated pass rate >= 92% on provided seed test set; fewer than 3 critical safety failures in manual review of 200 samples.

Attachments: sending a starter acceptance matrix and the sample prompt template (attached). Please add any additional prompts you want us to include.

Next steps / asks for Sunrise:
- Share the 1k sample prompts and any label mapping by Wed 6/3.
- Confirm preferred test windows (weekday morning PST and one evening slot) for the stress run.
- Sign off on the acceptance criteria or propose adjustments by end of day Fri 6/4.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with Ben and your team tomorrow.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks David — that matches our expectations and the timelines look doable. Two clarifications before we lock: 
1) For latency, the 512-token number is fine — our expected real-world median is ~220 tokens. Can Redwood also capture median and p99 in the readout?
2) For cost, our procurement needs a projected month-at-scale estimate assuming daily traffic at the baseline throughput.

We'll try to get the 1k prompts to you by Wednesday (some are still being redacted). If procurement needs a template for the SOW or cost appendix we can provide that.

Alicia

Subject: Re: Sunrise Health POC — success terms, ops handoff & acceptance routes

Adding a few technical notes that will affect observed KPIs and the acceptance gating: 
- Baseline model (fp16) will show higher per-token cost and slightly higher latency — expect a 15–25% improvement in both latency and cost when we enable batching + KV cache tuned to your session lengths.
- 4-bit quantization (Q4) typically reduces cost/token by ~35% but increases p99 tail by ~40–60ms depending on the kernel and hardware. We'll run both variants during Week 2 and include a recommended tradeoff table.
- For throughput runs we'll need a reproducible workload generator (we can run from our side if Sunrise prefers) and a short blocklist of prompt types that may trigger safety filters — if we hit safety rejects that will count toward the manual review failures.

Action items (Ben):
- Produce a short ‘‘tradeoff table’’ (latency vs cost vs quality) for the variants we test — due Fri 6/5.
- Generate projected monthly-cost workbook based on baseline hourly windows — due Thu 6/4.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — looking forward to the kickoff.
